derivation_notes: At low Reynolds number the dominant resistance is linear viscous (Stokes) drag proportional to speed, which coexists with the quadratic inertial drag that dominates at higher speeds; the total resistance is their sum.
change_summary: Added a linear viscous drag term -(linear_drag_coeff/mass)*v so that resistance transitions from Stokes-dominated at low speed to inertial-dominated at high speed, capturing the low-Reynolds regime the parent omitted.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: Viscous (Stokes) drag proportional to v dominates resistance at low speeds/low Reynolds number, while the existing quadratic inertial drag dominates at high speeds; the parent captures only the high-speed regime.

add_term_audit.observable_signature: During the early, slow phase of descent the acceleration is reduced more than pure quadratic drag predicts and the speed rises more gently; the terminal speed is lowered and no longer scales as sqrt(g*mass/drag_coeff).

derivation_notes: Real spheres exhibit a drag crisis: as speed (Reynolds number) rises past a critical value the boundary layer transitions from laminar to turbulent separation and the quadratic drag coefficient drops sharply. A tanh switch removes an extra low-speed drag contribution above the critical speed.
change_summary: Added a speed-gated extra quadratic drag term to the v-equation that is active in the subcritical regime and switches off (drag reduction) across a critical velocity, implementing the classic drag-crisis regime crossover.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: The dominant drag balance changes across a critical Reynolds/velocity threshold (the drag crisis), where laminar-to-turbulent boundary-layer transition abruptly lowers the effective quadratic drag coefficient.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: As drag_reduction_amp -> 0, or when drag_crisis_velocity is pushed far above all attained speeds so the tanh switch stays saturated (making the factor vanish over the operating range), the extra term disappears and the parent equation is recovered.

(2) The added-mass/buoyancy term written as (added_mass_coeff/mass)*g*tanh(v/velocity_scale) is unusual - added mass is classically a coefficient multiplying acceleration (dv/dt), not a velocity-saturating tanh of gravity. This is a non-standard, invented composite form. (3) The Basset history force classically appears as a convolution integral with a t^(-1/2) kernel; here it is replaced by an auxiliary relaxation state q with a single-mode ODE approximation - a genuinely non-classical closure. (5) The drag-crisis term with drag_reduction_amp*v**2*(1 - tanh((v - drag_crisis_velocity)/drag_crisis_width))/2 encodes a smooth speed-dependent reduction of drag through the drag crisis - a real physical phenomenon but never written in this precise closed-form composite. The complete combined ODE system with three coupled auxiliary states (v, w, q) and these specific tanh-based saturation/transition mechanisms does not appear in any known textbook or reference. No LLM could recite this exact formula from background knowledge; while individual physical concepts (Basset, added mass, drag crisis) are known, their specific mathematical realization here as coupled relaxation states and tanh switches is a data-driven construction. This represents genuine composite novelty beyond the classical baseline.
